- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent spike, but true outcome shows sharp drop or mean reversion, adjust downward early.
- After a price spike (e.g., >95), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or use exponential decay to smooth out.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.25), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate.
- Model frequently fails to capture true mean reversion after 3–5 consecutive high prices; add a 1–2 day lagged mean reversion buffer.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent trends; use 10-day moving average or weighted average of last 10 days to anchor forecast.
- If sentiment history shows no recent volatility, model tends to be too conservative; increase forecast by 3–5% to reflect hidden momentum.
